title: Comparison isomorphism of compact-support candidates along a refinement
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $c_i=(j_i,\bar f_i)$, $i=1,2$, be objects of the compactification category $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ and let $u:c_1\to c_2$ be a refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]: a proper $Y$-morphism $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with $\bar f_2\circ u=\bar f_1$ and $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Write $Rf_{!,n}^{c_i}=R\bar f_{i*,n}\,j_{i!}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the compact-support candidates [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], composed from the derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] on the small pro-etale sites. Let $(K,L,\alpha)$ be an object of $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$ [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], so that $K=\nu_X^*L$ with $L\in D^{+}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ through the witness $\alpha$. The *comparison isomorphism along $u$* is the morphism

$$
 \theta_u(K):
 Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}K=R\bar f_{1*,n}\,j_{1!}K
 \xrightarrow{\ c_{\bar f_2,u}\ }
 R\bar f_{2*,n}\,Ru_{*,n}\,j_{1!}K
 \xrightarrow{\ R\bar f_{2*,n}(\alpha_u^{-1})\ }
 R\bar f_{2*,n}\,j_{2!}K=Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}K,
$$

where $c_{\bar f_2,u}:R(\bar f_2\circ u)_{*,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_{2*,n}\circ Ru_{*,n}$ is the composition isomorphism of derived direct images at finite level [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], applied to $\bar f_1=\bar f_2\circ u$, and $\alpha_u:j_{2!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{*,n}\,j_{1!}K$ is the canonical isomorphism of the proper-open comparison for complexes from the etale site [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale], applied to the proper morphism $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ of Noetherian schemes (they are of finite type over the field $K_0$), the open immersions $j_1,j_2$ with $u\circ j_1=j_2$, and $K=\nu_X^*L$ (that lemma is stated for the derived direct image and extension by zero of the proper-base-change chapter [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; these are the same constructions, by a K-injective resolution and by sheafifying the presheaf equal to the given module on objects factoring through the open and to $0$ otherwise, as [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and [def-weil-extension-by-zero]). Being a composite of two isomorphisms, $\theta_u(K)$ is an isomorphism; it is natural in $(K,L,\alpha)$, so that $\theta_u:Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}$ is a natural isomorphism of functors $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The witness of $K$ is carried along: $\theta_u$ is defined on the object $(K,L,\alpha)$, not on $K$ alone. That $\theta_u$ is the identity for the identity refinement and that $\theta_{v\circ u}=\theta_v\circ\theta_u$ for composable refinements are not part of this definition; they are the first assertions of the compactification-coherence proposition (node prop-compactification-coherence-detailed, which is not cited here as a dependency since it is stated in terms of this comparison).

source.place: node prop-compactification-coherence-detailed, order 1485, statement: 'the canonical transformation between the compact-support candidates $R\bar f_{1*,n}j_{1!}\to R\bar f_{2*,n}j_{2!}$ is the composite of the proper-composition isomorphism with the isomorphism $Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}$ on the ambient derived category', and its proof, steps 1-2 ($\alpha_u^{-1}$ from lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale, $R\bar f_{1*,n}\simeq R\bar f_{2*,n}Ru_*$ from lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition (1)); cited by node def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, order 1486, as 'the natural comparison isomorphism $Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}$ induced by proper composition and extension by zero'
